Based on my search, here's what I found about the browser-use Cloud API's browser client, CDP URL, and authentication:

## Authentication Header

The key detail confirmed across multiple sources is the custom auth header. The auth header name is `X-Browser-Use-API-Key`. Using `Authorization: Bearer ...` silently fails with a generic 401.

In practice, the REST client sets up headers like this:
REST uses a custom header (not `Authorization: Bearer` — that path returns a generic 401 silently): `HEADERS = { "X-Browser-Use-API-Key": os.environ["BROWSER_USE_API_KEY"], "Content-Type": "application/json" }`. The key only authorises actions on browsers and profiles created under it — there are no organisation-level admin endpoints on the public API.

## Creating a Browser & Getting the CDP URL

Using the official SDK, you create a browser and connect to it via CDP: with the Python SDK you call `client.browsers.create()`, then connect over CDP with `p.chromium.connect_over_cdp(browser.cdp_url)`, and stop with `client.browsers.stop(browser.id)`. In TypeScript, you connect via `puppeteer.connect({ browserWSEndpoint: browser.cdpUrl })`.

Note the field naming difference: the Python SDK exposes `cdp_url` while the raw API/TypeScript object uses `cdpUrl`.

## Important cdpUrl Gotchas (from cloud.py / harness notes)

- `start_remote_daemon` overwrites `BU_CDP_WS` in the daemon env; re-read from `browser["cdpUrl"]` if you need the value afterwards. (PR #300 stops run.py from clobbering an explicit `BU_CDP_URL`, but the daemon env still gets set.)
- On stopping a browser: the body is `{"action": "stop"}`. It returns 200 with the same browser object, but `liveUrl` and `cdpUrl` come back as null and `finishedAt` is populated. Use the returned `proxyCost` + `browserCost` for the final cost.
- The `liveUrl` host is `live.browser-use.com`, not `cloud.browser-use.com` — they're separate surfaces.

## SDK & Connection Reference

From the browser-use cloud skill docs: Auth header: `X-Browser-Use-API-Key: <key>`; get API key at https://cloud.browser-use.com/new-api-key; set env var `BROWSER_USE_API_KEY=<key>`. Cloud SDK installs via `uv pip install browser-use-sdk` (Python) or `npm install browser-use-sdk` (TypeScript). The CDP WebSocket endpoint is `wss://connect.browser-use.com?apiKey=KEY&proxyCountryCode=us`.

The API base URLs are: `https://api.browser-use.com/api/v2/` (v2) or `https://api.browser-use.com/api/v3` (v3).

## Other Field-Handling Notes

A couple of data-type caveats worth noting when parsing responses in cloud.py:
- Cost fields are strings, not numbers — `proxyCost`, `browserCost`, `proxyUsedMb` come back as quoted strings (e.g. "0.0123"); cast to float before arithmetic.
- `cookieDomains` can be `None` on freshly-created profiles; guard with `c or []`.
- `_browser_use` has a 60s timeout in admin.py; long-running ops (large profile sync) need their own polling.

I've implemented cloud browser support in browser-use, matching the source of the upstream feature (PR #3139). Here's what I did:

## Changes

**`browser_use/browser/cloud.py`** (new file)
- `CloudBrowserResponse` — pydantic model with `id`, `status`, `cdpUrl`, `liveUrl`, `timeoutAt`, `startedAt`, `finishedAt`.
- `CloudBrowserError` / `CloudBrowserAuthError` (the latter subclasses the former).
- `CloudBrowserClient`:
  - `create_browser()` — `POST {base}/api/v2/browsers` with the `X-Browser-Use-API-Key` header. API key is read from `BROWSER_USE_API_KEY` first, then falls back to `CloudAuthConfig.load_from_file()`. Raises `CloudBrowserAuthError` mentioning the env var when no key is found, and on HTTP 401 raises `CloudBrowserAuthError('Authentication failed…')`. Stores `current_session_id`.
  - `stop_browser(session_id=None)` — `PATCH {base}/api/v2/browsers/{id}` with `{'action': 'stop'}`; raises `CloudBrowserError('…not found')` on HTTP 404.
  - `close()` for cleanup.
- Module-level `get_cloud_browser_cdp_url()`, `stop_cloud_browser_session()`, and `cleanup_cloud_client()` using a lazily-created global client.

**`browser_use/browser/profile.py`**
- Added `use_cloud` field (defaults to `True` when `BROWSER_USE_API_KEY` is set) plus a `cloud_browser` alias property. Setting `use_cloud=True` leaves `is_local` at its `False` default.

- Added `cloud_browser` property returning `browser_profile.use_cloud`.

- On stop: cleans up the cloud session.

**`CloudAuthConfig`** already existed in `browser_use/sync/auth.py` with `api_token`/`user_id`/`authorized_at`, `save_to_file()`, `load_from_file()`, and `BROWSER_USE_CONFIG_DIR`-based location — no changes needed.
